atoms.lesson:
### Intuition
In many versions of **inflation**, that runaway expansion never completely ends. It halts in some patches — which become universes like ours — but keeps going elsewhere, sprouting new bubbles forever. That would make our universe one bubble among countless others: a **multiverse**. Whether this is real science or untestable speculation is fiercely argued, even among inflation's inventors.

### Precisely
**Eternal inflation** is the result that, in many inflaton potentials, *quantum* fluctuations of the field outpace its classical rolling in some regions, so those regions keep inflating while others exit and reheat into **pocket universes**. Combined with the **string-theory landscape** (an estimated $\sim10^{500}$ metastable vacua), different pockets could have different effective constants of physics — a genuine **multiverse**.

### Worked example
Consider the "anthropic" argument for the **cosmological-constant**: its observed value is $\sim10^{120}$ times smaller than naive expectation. In a multiverse where $\Lambda$ varies pocket to pocket, only pockets with small $\Lambda$ form galaxies and observers — so we *must* find ourselves in one. Weinberg used this reasoning in 1987 to predict $\Lambda$ should be small but nonzero, before its 1998 discovery — a rare case where multiverse logic made a (controversial) prediction.

### Why it's true / how it works
The trouble is the **measure problem**: with infinitely many pockets, computing "the probability of observing X" requires a way to count infinities, and different counting schemes give wildly different answers. Worse, if anything happens *somewhere*, the framework risks predicting nothing — threatening **falsifiability**, a basic requirement of science.

### Where it connects
It is a direct extrapolation of **inflation** and intertwines with the anthropic interpretation of the **cosmological-constant** fine-tuning.

### Watch out
This is the most *philosophically* loaded atom in the branch. Critics (including some original inflation architects) argue a theory predicting "anything can happen somewhere" makes no testable predictions; defenders point to possible bubble-collision imprints in the CMB — *none observed*. Treat it as an open, partly philosophical debate, not established physics.

atoms.title: The ultimate fate of the universe
atoms.summary: If dark energy is a constant, the universe expands forever toward a cold, empty, isolated future.

depths.eli5: How the universe ends depends almost entirely on dark energy. If it keeps pushing space apart at a steady rate, galaxies drift ever farther apart, stars eventually run out of fuel and burn out, and the cosmos coasts into a dark, cold, empty, lonely future. But if dark energy behaves differently than we think, stranger endings become possible.
depths.core: Dark energy sets the long-term fate of the universe. If dark energy is a true cosmological constant (w = −1, steady forever), expansion accelerates without end: distant galaxies are carried beyond our 'event horizon' (the boundary past which their light can never reach us again), new star formation eventually stops, and everything fades toward a cold, dilute 'heat death' — a universe so spread out and uniform that nothing more can happen. Two alternatives hinge on dark energy's equation-of-state w: if w < −1 ('phantom energy,' even more repulsive), the acceleration runs away into a 'Big Rip' that eventually tears apart galaxies, stars, and atoms; if dark energy instead weakens over time, the expansion could slow or even reverse into a future collapse.
depths.deep: Under ΛCDM, in tens of billions of years the accelerating expansion will redshift all galaxies outside the Local Group beyond our cosmological event horizon — a far-future observer would see an empty sky and could not deduce the Big Bang, a sobering note on the contingency of cosmic knowledge.

atoms.lesson:
### Intuition
How the universe ends depends almost entirely on dark energy. If it keeps pushing space apart at a steady rate, galaxies drift ever farther apart, stars run out of fuel and burn out, and the cosmos coasts into a dark, cold, empty, lonely future. But if dark energy behaves differently than we think, stranger endings become possible.

### Precisely
The **ultimate fate** hinges on the **dark-energy-equation-of-state** $w$:
- $w = -1$ (true **cosmological-constant**): eternal accelerated expansion toward **heat death** — a cold, maximally entropic, dilute universe where no work can be done.
- $w < -1$ (**phantom energy**): density *grows*, ending in a **Big Rip** that tears apart clusters, galaxies, stars, then atoms at a finite future time.
- $w$ weakening over time: expansion could slow or reverse into a collapse ("Big Crunch").

### Worked example
Under ΛCDM, the **event horizon** in physical terms is $d_{\text{eh}} = c/H_\infty$ where $H_\infty = \sqrt{\Lambda c^2/3}$. In tens of billions of years, every galaxy outside the gravitationally bound **Local Group** will redshift beyond this horizon and vanish from view. A far-future astronomer would see an empty sky and could not deduce the **big-bang** or the **cmb-origin** at all — cosmic knowledge is *contingent on when you look*.

### Why it's true / how it works
A constant $\Lambda$ makes $H \to H_\infty = $ const, so $a \propto e^{H_\infty t}$ — exponential, like a late-time **inflation**. Anything not gravitationally bound is carried across the event horizon and causally severed. Star formation ends as gas is exhausted, and the universe cools toward maximum entropy.

### Where it connects
It is the long-term extrapolation of **lambda-cdm** and **dark-energy**, gated by the **observable-universe** horizon and decided by the **dark-energy-equation-of-state**.

### Watch out
"Heat death" does not mean the universe gets hot — quite the opposite: it grows ever colder and more dilute. The name refers to thermodynamic *heat* (energy) becoming uniformly spread so no gradients remain to do work, i.e. maximum entropy.

atoms.lesson:
### Intuition
This atom puts every chapter into one timeline. In order: a flash of **inflation** in the first instant; a few minutes of nuclear cooking forging the light elements; the clearing of the cosmic fog 380,000 years in (releasing the CMB); the slow gravitational building of galaxies and the cosmic web over billions of years; and finally, in recent cosmic times, **dark-energy** taking the wheel and accelerating expansion. One coherent $\sim13.8$-billion-year story.

### Precisely
The standard chronology, with characteristic times, redshifts, and temperatures (via **thermal-history**, $T \propto 1+z$):
- **Inflation** ($t \sim 10^{-34}\,\text{s}$): quantum seeds stretched; flatness and uniformity set.
- **Baryogenesis**: tiny matter surplus $\eta \approx 6\times10^{-10}$.
- **BBN** ($t \sim 1$–$200\,\text{s}$, $T \sim 10^{9}\,\text{K}$): $^4$He, D, $^7$Li forged.
- **Recombination** ($t \approx 380{,}000\,\text{yr}$, $z\approx1100$, $T\approx3000\,\text{K}$): CMB released.
- **Structure formation** (millions–billions of yr): the **large-scale-structure** cosmic web grows.
- **Dark-energy domination** ($z \lesssim 0.7$): accelerated expansion begins.

### Worked example
Cross-check two epochs with one tool. At **recombination**, $T = 2.725 \times 1101 \approx 3000\,\text{K}$. At **bbn**, the same $T \propto 1+z$ relation with $T \sim 10^9\,\text{K}$ gives $z \sim 4\times10^8$. The *single* scaling law placing both epochs consistently is a small example of the framework's internal coherence.

### Why it's true / how it works
The deep point is not merely that each stage is independently evidenced — it is that the *same six* **lambda-cdm** parameters that fit the **cmb-anisotropies** also predict the **bbn** abundances, the **baryon-acoustic-oscillations** scale, and the supernova **standard-candles** distance–redshift relation. Cross-validation across vastly different epochs and physics is what elevates this from a story to a tested model.

### Where it connects
This atom ties together the entire branch: **inflation**, **bbn**, **recombination**, **cmb-origin**, **gravitational-instability**, **large-scale-structure**, and **dark-energy** — the unified narrative behind **lambda-cdm**, with open edges at the **hubble-tension** and **dark-energy-equation-of-state**.

### Watch out
The coherence is real but the model is *incomplete*: dark matter and dark energy — about 95% of the budget — remain unidentified, and the earliest pre-BBN instants rely on unverified physics. A tested framework is not a finished one.
